content: A plastic prop that was found at the foot of the rubbish mountain. Kuzumi is trying her best to practice the art of wizardry. She is hoping to one day cast a spell to put smiles on everyone's faces.

name: [Item] Scavenger Token
content: A Scavenger Token can be obtained by registering at District One Central Recycling Station. It seems that such identification exists in every well, just as a stamp collection in theme parks.\nIf it was a theme park, there should be a way to quickly escape.

name: [Item] Hoodoo Map
content: A dynamic map Gino made by utilising the Saturn Permission. It records people's activities within the Hoodoo over the course of three days. Just as he had expected, the scavengers haven't violated any of the rules presented to them.

name: [Rec] Beggar's Chicken
content:
Beggar's Chicken is a traditional pre-disaster cuisine. The whole chicken was marinated, then covered with soil or flour, wrapped with a lotus leaf, and finally grilled on a stove. This would secure its juiciness entirely, ensuring the chicken to be fresh and tender, as well as a crispy golden skin. The original recipe is very strict about the ingredients. Due to the geographical restrictions, Gino used the wild green-haired chicken, battery soil with excessive metallic contents, and tin foil instead.

Searching for delicacies seems to be the mission I was born for. Wherever I go, I would always be indulged in the local cuisines. All around the world, every cuisine cultures, from luxurious dishes to refreshing desserts --- where there is the delicious food, there is me. That's me, Geopelia the super gourmet. Welcome to my Tasty Food Review channel! [background: yeah!!!!]
Now let's interview our special guest today, Chief Gino!
You have anything to say to our audience, Chief?
[Crunching, Gino held the 'giant rock', focusing on crushing it onto the ground, totally ignoring Geopelia, and murmuring to himself: "this crap isn't even canon..."]Hmm......Chief, what dish are we making today?
[Gino looked up at Geopelia, remembering that he still had a chisel in his mouth, then signaled to Geopelia to take the green juice beside, and made a drinking gesture.]
Asking me to drink it? [It tasted a bit bitter] What is this thing?
[Relaxed his bite and spoke] 'Antidote.'
!!!!!
The chicken was quite tasty though.

name: [Rec] Mutant Poultry
content: A specimen belonging to a mutated species of now extinct birds, noticed by Gino and Geopelia in the landfill of District Eight. It has eight legs and six wings. It is known as the "green peafowl" by the local residents, despite not belonging to the same genus. It is wrongly believed that the species is a result of genetically enhanced poultry created by an ancient "fast-food" chain being exposed to, and adapting to the harsh post-disaster environment.\n[Limbo Wiki]: Soup based on the creature's feathers can help against heavy metal poisoning.

name: [Image] Water Tower
content: The life-sustaining structures scattered around the Hoodoo. Each tower is marked with complex patterns and local serial numbers by local residents. The pattern on the joint railing of the District Eight water tower depicts an eight-legged horse with an infinity symbol etched into its back. Each tower is roughly 30 meters tall and measures 8 meters in diameter. The towers are made up of a large cylinder containing 4 smaller ones, three of which are designated purification systems, with the last one being the storage tank. The purifying installation has two inlets, for air and polluted water, and five outlets for purified water that flows into the storage tank, and the others for the remaining chemical compounds that are pumped into a waste container. The waste is then pumped down into the energy network, where violent chemical reactions are turned into power for sustaining the entire circulatory system.

name: Trophon - Clue IV
content:
With the help of some scavengers, Trophon's tires and rear-view mirrors were replaced, and a makeshift broadcasting system was installed.
Kouma: Test. Test. Trophon, do you copy?
Geopelia: Roger. Awaiting orders.
Kouma: Engine - start!
Geopelia: Top gear!
Gino: You're getting a bit too excited....
Geopelia: Accompany me for a lap, Gino!
Gino: Okay, hold on tight, don't get blown away!
[Trophon's engine roared, Geopelia felt the behemoth's powerful roar underneath her body, and lifted her feet off the ground. The sudden acceleration made her panic fora bit, and she instinctively tightened her grasp around Gino, and secretly closed her eyes. And with that the two vanished into the Hoodoo.]

name: The Alpa Pen - Clue IV
content: Geopelia has recently developed a strange habit. After writing down a journal entry, she will modify its frequency and insert it into the entry itself. If you hear bizarre noises, you might consider cracking it.

name: The Alpa Pen - Clue V
content:
In the middle of the night, Alpa assumed a physical form and sneaked out of the pen. It was found and apprehended by  Kuzumi, who at the time was painting in the hallway. So the two spent a pleasant fantasy night together.
Kuzumi: Where did this kitten come from? So cute~
Alpa: Woof!
Kuzumi: A bark?!
[Kuzumi suddenly felt enlightened, held Alpa up and began shouting]
Kuzumi: I understood now! You are a divine gift bestowed upon me by the goddess of inspiration!
Alpa: Meow~
[Alpa latched onto Kuzumi's thigh and let out a moan. Kuzumi's head was bursting with ideas, her little notepad gradually getting filled with page after page of adventures of Alpa the cat. Kuzumi had a feeling, that this would have made for a great picture book series.]

name: [Rec] Morning
content:
Awaken by the sound of Gino's flute, Geopelia opened the terminal. Alpa is still analyzing File 377. Each faint of an unfamiliar name on the list remains unheared from. She took out her notepad, wrote down the date and started covertly recording her morning.
[4th of April, sunny
It is the fourth day since we mounted the Tower. With the help of the scavengers, we are gradually starting to understand the Hoodoos, and the new world. We set up a temporary home in District Eight.
The Hoodoo are so quiet, just like Glaciaxia in the past, however I am fearful of this just being the calm before the storm. Before we left, the notes from Captain Dlyro mentioned that, the collapse phenomenon is an untamed beast; greed being its nature, it would bite on any and all living things in its sight. After the fall of Glaciaxia, the Hoodoos would follow; then, all of the Tower's worlds would not be able to escape that fate.
But can our story really end like this?]

name: [Rec] Morning - Clue I
content: "Breakfast is ready. Come here and eat."\n"Coming, coming!"

name: [Item] Five-Color Rock
content: End result of the petroleum rivers' existance. It is smooth to the touch, and will reflect a spectrum of colors when exposed to sunlight. The south river bank is so saturated with the rocks that they form a beach stretching all the way to the Tuhun Waterfall.\n[Limbo Wiki]: The Tuhun Waterfall is directly connected to the Judgment Channel flowing into the Endless Sea of Bailin. There lives a large amount of whims that swim upstream from the Endless Sea. Adventurers, please avoid the Tuhun Waterfall unless absolutely necessary.

name: [File] Colorful Picture Book
content: A file stored on Alpa. It is a hand-painted picture book, illustrated with vivid colors. The story while somewhat incoherent, seems to be about the adventures of a barking kitten in a place called Rainbow Falls, and its encounters various magical creatures.

name: [Item] Metal Arm
content: Found on an abandoned bridge connecting two sides of the petroleum river. Like a fish out of water, it lets its morphological top and bottom swing freely back and forth nonstop until the luminous body of energy reaches the top of the celestial sphere, impelling the fingers, standing upright on the ground and travelling faraway.\n"It seems edible... [Thinking.png]"

name: [Item] Bitter Nuts
content: These organic treats can help reduce excessive energy flow in the body. They can also be used as an alternative energy source for Alpa. [Inadvisable operation, shouldn't be imitated under any circumstances]\nThe nuts are manufactured by the denisens of District Two, next to the stream. After Alpa finished its analysis, Geopelia decided to quickly bury the disgusting snack in the sand under the water tower of District Eight.

name: Radio - Clue III
content:
Fuli: And there, good as new! Now if only I could deliver it to Kuzumi... Damn, I still have so much work...
Geopelia: I can give it to her!
Fuli: Really? Oh, Geopelia, I love you!
Gino: Hum? Give you what to whom?
[Gino just came back from intelligence gathering. It was a windy night, and Gino's hair was a mess. He tried to fix it, but ultimately messed it up even more.]
Gino: C'mon now, if you look like a kid, then you are a kid. Act accordingly, and go to bed.
Geopelia: Muuu~

In her memory, there was someone, who let go of her hand, boarded a train, and never turned back. She is still waiting for that train, hoping to show that person the picture book she has painted as an expression of her forgotten childhood, hoping to see them once again.

name: [Item] Anchor
content:
Ash floated in the viscous sea. The hundred-story-high anchor blocks the blinding sunrays. The giant "JUSTICE" intaglio was covered in dark oily stains. He looked at the dim orange sky, contemplating how did it ever come to this.  He isn't given much time to think, as Findstr, who lowered himself on an anchor, reached for his hand. His overly pale face and white hair were gleaming in the sunlight. "Don't put your guard down just yet, there is still danger lurking in the darkness."
"When will it be safe to escape?" Ash was leaning on Findstr out of exhaustion.
"I don't know. But-" Findstr stood up and started walking away "I suggest you don't turn around."
He felt a sudden tremor. A wave pushed against his back, riffled his fingers, and climbed up his wrist. Ash didn't dare to look down and examine the hot, pricking sensation. He staggered and ran in Findstr's direction. The fact that the melting feeling  disappeared after he started running didn't comfort him at all. He caught up to Findstr, and saw the anchor in his smile.
The oily clumps were slowly oozing down to the ground, like a person's skin peeling away, like a dress wriggling in the sea, made out of countless muddy hands.
Findstr said, "There is nowhere safe to run in this world. Not for people like us. The evils of the surface will roam under under the sun, comfortable in their domain."

name: [Image] Fortress
content:
"As we were driving through the central area of District Ten, an enormous city-sized fortress appeared in front of us. Different from the concrete honeycomb-shaped pillar complexes we have seen prior, its giant main arch stood menacingly on the valley floor, with hundreds of signaling towers attached to the cliff below. The distress signal I received shows that its source was slowly moving outwards from the fortress' gate. My instincts told me not to act recklessly, as I wasn't familiar with the fortress's internal architecture, and the distress signal's low level indicated no threat to anyone's life.
While I was trying to come up with a plan, Geopelia started taking photos of everything. She stood on the motorcycle, joyfully exclaiming that she had a nice angle. She has been acting like this ever since we had arrived in the hoodos. Sceneries, people, monuments, anything that herself, and was within her range, she had to capture. She says she's doing some kind of an album, as if we didn't have any actually important things to tend to... It all feels like some game to her.
Since her camera can see further than the naked eye, I asked her to check whether there was somebody at the gate. Surprisingly she didn't argue, and I heard the shutter click.
"Gino, something came out."
"From which side??"
"From the sky-"
She pointed upwards. A black dot was flying towards us, constantly reforming its shape. The second it appeared from behind the horizon, the original distress signal has ceased. In its stead, countless other distress signals appeared on the map.
"Run!"
I grabbed Geopelia, jumped on Trophon's seat, and rushed away the scene. 
"Gino! They're closing in! Speed Up! I stepped on the gas, but suddenly I couldn't feel Geopelia's heat on my back. In looked in the rear view mirror. She didn't fall, she was just leaning back, looking through her camera.
"Stop taking pictures! You are gonna fall off!"
"They- they stopped..."
The flock seemed to not be abe to leave perimeter of the valley, but I still didn't dare to deccelerate until we left the district. Geopelia seemed concerned. I asked her what was on her mind.
She was looking throught the pictures she took, but then stopped, turned to me, and exclaimed "It's better to be a real person".

name: Perchnest Station - Clue I
content:
Kouma was standing on the platform, overseeing countless enormous pillars, almost grazing the sky. Nine red suns were scattered along the tracks. Not too long before, everything was shining in the burning sunlight, the flora was torched, the land was barren, the people were dying of starvation. Now things are different, the world reversing its course and contorting at will. Kouma let out a sad sigh.
Geopelia wasn't able to sleep in the makeshift bed the scavengers set up for her. She got up early, and thought that she might as well get out and watch the dawn, without alerting Gino. 
“Good morning Kouma.”
“Young lady came for sunrise?”
“Yeah...  Kuzumi hasn't shown up today?”
“She didn't. But you, do you really want to settle down in District Eight? ”
 “No. Once we find the entrance to the third floor, we are leaving.”
“Just like Kuzumi's brother, huh... He didn't return. Left her behind. But it's hard to judge him. After what happened, very few people remained in the Hoodoos... ”

name: Warrior – One – Horse
content:
Glaciaxia-53.A.P

"Hold the reins, get familiar with the horse's breathing, and imagine where you want to go."
On a day in winter, she's teaching "me" the method to control the ghast horse. "I" closed my eyes, imagined the drifting snow, and floating phantom in the distance, then opened my eyes.
"I can't do it."
"What did you see?"
"I" closed my eyes once more. The snow had stopped. The sun set like a horde of migratory wild geese heading towards north, cirrocumulus clouds scattered around it. He stood in the air, streams of clouds flew by his side. The giant tower hung upside down in the sky. Its flesh was made of whims and bones of steel. "I" looked at the tower, and the residents of the tower looked at him, stopped cultivating. A cold light of reflection flashed from the blade of their rusty scythes. 
"I, saw nothing."

name: Warrior – Two – Dashing
content:
Glaciaxia-57.A.P

The iron horseshoes of the ghast horse splashed out snowy mists as we sped along the mountain ridgeline. Scout ghosts chased closely behind us, with their misty bodies hovering over the ground. Ahead of us was a bottomless cliff, which would surely be our doom if fell into. But all "my" attention were on her long hair, which flew out of the gaps of her helmet, and with marvellous ice crystals weaving over them.
"Use the Melt! We jump over the cliff!"
"My" mind is filled with the back of her, while the wild wind suddenly paused and rose up again, before we were standing on the tip of the mountain behind the cliff.
She took off her helmet, gazing towards the giant tower faraway. Even the tower base under construction was already high up into the clouds. She sighed.
"They have abandoned their homeland, and they will again abandon the world in the tower in the future."
Upon finishing the last syllable, she disappeared from where she was.

name: Warrior – Three – Comedy
content:
Glaciaxia-59.A.P

"I", the man in the court, sat in the middle of the dome theatre, with both hands cuffed behind the chair, like a naked beast, trapped for display. This is the first theatre trial since the launch of the Tower project. Thousands of people – men and women, old and young, filled up the tiny theatre, like people who casually watch beheadings on their way for groceries in the old days.
The solemn trials had been tarnished in this time. The fate of suspects had all been fixed, and the trials are more of recreations to please the public, who are increasingly deprived of entertainment. Before the trail starts, the judge always plays Sunrise by Strauss just pretending to be arty, since it was the first disc they dug up from the trash piles. After the song, the judge would start to read out all the crimes of the person in court, and the jury would outrageously demand for death penalty, and not letting any person with such great sins to see the sunrise of tomorrow.
Each of them wearing an angry red mask of justice. The men in court mobilised their facial muscles, and smiled with their greatest respect.
The men in court had no right to answer. It is the newly born tradition of the era that the jailer cut the tongue of prisoners on death row. The criminals on court had no chance to speak, so keeping their tongues were simply a waste, might as well provide a better meal for the ghast horses. This jailer was very thoughtful, and used some glue to help "me" stopped the bleeding. Still remembered drinking the sticky liquid. A stream of warmth rushed up my heart and, I, did not feel heart anywhere anymore.
While the judge announced the lengthy trial results, only one person left early. The back of that person looked extremely similar to hers, no, that was her! The men in the court got up trying to catch the captain’s shadow, but unknowingly tripped "me" to the ground, unaware of the chains on the feet.
The jury burst into laughter. At this moment who else would know, that “I” used to be a warriror.

name: Warrior – Four – Glaciaxia
content:
Glaciaxia-60.A.P

The sky and earth shared the same colour, white and vague. The prisoners kneeled on the ground, humming the ancient tone.
Air stripped away his body heat, and the hyperthermia deprived his thoughts. The photoreceptor cells twisted and struggled to function. The darkness in his eyes glowed with light. The recklessly writhing monsters with human faces, are appearing into reality, or his dreams.
"……"
Say something, say something! Tell him, that in the world of Glaciaxia, there were still men breathing, that the poem of life was still being chanted. And the homeland they stood up to. People built the tower not just to leave, they just, just……
"You are going to die, just like us, put to death by human."
"There is no future, but wandering forever, on the snowy field, over and over again, reincarnating."
"Just like."

name: Warrior – Five - Launching
content:

"The main Tower body is about to launch from the surface. All personnel please check your secure attachment measures. Repeat. The main Tower body is about to launch from the surface. All personnel please check your secure attachment measures."
The snow stopped. The giant silhouette of the Tower appeared, and shrank again in the passage of time. The snowy field shook, herds of beasts ran, teared, hunt, and chased, leaving irregular trials behind on the new snows. They gathered, piled, flattened, and bulged in the deep pit where the tower had left, like a bloating cow belly, digesting. Inveracity and eccentricity rose in people’s minds.
People left, but should they really have done so. The collective suicides of the whims are as always, the revolt against human, or the final, kind warning.

name: [Image] Clock Paradox
content:
The spaceship steps into the depth of the universe, as its engine rumbles. The mining machines wander among the asteroid belt off the racetrack. Viewing far out to the south pole of Saturn, there is a giant clock face, so profound as the eye of the white whole. The spaceship of the first men, Ark I, stops here, in the still time, falling back occasionally as a mirage.
From the distance to the near, countless needles with unknown scales rotates slowly, clockwise or anticlockwise. Some stays in silence for years without moving for one second, while others move as swiftly as photons, spin and sink from the highest point, falling into the far depth of the inner core.
Those needles are nearly identical, all connected in series by the pole, maintaining the clockwork in an incomprehensible way. Perhaps the only clock needle we see has always been that same one, while the others are mere fading phantoms, filling in the gaps of the real numbers, and then become nameless new real number scales, until no longer divisible.
The seemingly never-stopping time appears like a view of moving frames. It stays still at its smallest scale, yet relative to the observers, the stillness obtains the nature of movement. Whether it is due to the movement or the stillness of the observer, we are yet to know.
This is the clock paradox.

name: About: Pixel Tower
content: The now-slumbering world of mutual understanding, a spiritual sanctuary mankind wove for themselves. Much of the information connected to it no longer warrants an introduction, but what you might’ve not known is that it was the centerpiece of Project PhigrOS: a simulator, a virtual world woven from the collective subconscious. Its birth carried no poetic color, but the ideals it carried never faded away.

name: About: Limbo
content: The far shore represents reality, and the Pixel Tower symbolizes illusion.\nThose of you still reading these words in this place are Limbos - awakened souls who know their bodies exist in another parallel world.

name: About: Vault
content: The hypothetical tenth floor of the Pixel Tower. The deepest of one’s heart where every secret reside within. Because the Pixel Tower existed, people's minds could touch one another, and one person's Vault could connect to another's.\nIt was the connection of countless Vaults that made the Vault's existence possible as a floor. But when the Mazarine End arrived, the Vault shattered into countless fragments, and each person became an islet of the mind once more.

name: About: Mazarine End
content: The Mazarine End marks the boundary between Mazarine and other spaces, manifesting as a line that devours data. When it sweeps across, everything vanishes, reducing all to darkness not unlike a skydog devouring the moon.\nAll memories eventually reach Mazarine. It is the logic underlying the Pixel Tower, and only what is left after it shuts down.

name: About: Collections
content: For most of the Tower's history, people compressed myths, contamination, and ravings into standardized currencies, exchanged at fixed denominations. These are the "collectibles" we see so often. Whole or broken, when traded as currency, they are called data - the materialized form of undifferentiated human mental labor.

name: [Decipher] About The Universe - Clue I
content: In 2089, Project PhigrOS launched. An organization called the "Tower", relying on the medical facilities of the Jiangyuan Base, implanted nanobionic machines into every registered resident. Utilizing these machines, along with the signal stations spread across the base, they created a shared subconscious world for humanity; which came to be known as the "Pixel Tower". \nThe experiment, with an intention to reverse-engineer their lost civilization, reverted the entire world's time to 2019, reconstructing it in the process. As the simulation's time approached 2089, people began to question a future they had never reached. Thus, the "Whims", a strange phenomena born entirely from the collective imagination, appeared. \nThere were too many unknowns in the subconscious world. The experiment slipped beyond the Tower organization's control, and they could not stop it.

name: Peregrinus's Notebook - Clue I
content:
During most breaks in the exploration, that young scholar would spread the thin notebook on his lap and jot across the loose sheets tucked inside. A slender pen held in his thick, heavy gloves still moved lightly and nimbly, filling more than half a page in a flash.
 At first I paid it little mind. Only when I learned he had made a name for himself in the computational sciences did I grow curious. A man so familiar with electronic devices had chosen the most primitive paper records - how strange. I couldn't help paying attention to his actions.
 Was it because I saw it so often that I failed to notice it getting thicker? I once wondered about this, and he keenly caught the thought. The answer was unexpected: most of it wasn't worth writing down, so the pages hadn't really grown. Peregrinus answered with a smile - a sigh of regret, or maybe a murmur to himself. The sheets were closed together with the notebook and lifted, swaying slightly in the cold wind; his handwriting was fine and delicate. Out of respect for his privacy, I turned away, but he saw through me again. In the corner of my eye, he was beaming.
 
 "You don't have to look away. Only pigeons can ever read them."
 Why did he make it sound like he was calming a child?

name: Peregrinus's Notebook - Clue II
content:
"Actually, I heard it all - you were discussing how to find me over the radio."
"Then why didn't you come out sooner?"
As always, Peregrinus took on the advance search work - in my name, of course, accompanying me as partner and adviser. Experienced, quick, and meticulous, he finished tasks very fast, pouring the extra time into his own interests and research. At times like that, I had no choice but to follow him. If he didn't want me tagging along, he would vanish after a quick hello and reappear at muster time. That was the case this time - with a few surprises.
"I'm just confident in my judgment. If this building really was used for... Ah, time to go. If you want to hear the rest, I'll tell you later. Same as always - cover for me if anyone asks why."
Before I could nod, Peregrinus was already heading outside. The medics, scholars, and guards swarmed around him, patting and examining him. I was two steps late but still caught in the crowd, swept along toward camp.

name: Peregrinus's Notebook - Clue III
content:
At dusk the snow stopped. The wind had died down from daytime but still howled through. I climbed a low ridge, and at the cliff's edge the side of the building came into view - nearly a third of it had collapsed. The rock below jutted out like a hawk's beak, its broken edges pale gray in the twilight.
"Every trace I've found points to this having been a fairly large research base."
Peregrinus came over too. He raised a finger and swept it across a considerable area of the cold, patchy fog drifting below the cliff.
"Inside it, thousands of AIs reside in all kinds of media - organizing, driving, managing, providing humans with everything they need."
"Can artificial intelligence really reach that level?" I asked in doubt.
"Decades ago, yes." Peregrinus leaned closer and lowered his voice. "...The technology of that time... was enough to grant AI most of the traits humans have - appearance, thought, even soul. They had long since blended quietly into human society and life, filling the gaps in middle and lower positions. That wasn't a 'problem' at first. But when the ice age came and resources dwindled, it became a 'problem' again. But-"
"But?"
I looked at him and saw a conviction burning in those golden eyes, tightly wrapped in worries.
"Ah, don't be nervous." Something occurred to Peregrinus and he suddenly smiled. "I just thought of my little sister. I often do this when I tell her bedtime stories."
He moved away, closer to the cliff, and continued.
"If this were a story, what comes next would be artificial intelligence making a mistake and destroying everything until nothing was left. Unfortunately, that's not how it went. This base was hidden so deep, and yet it still became a casualty of the world war - it was humans who destroyed it."
A predictable outcome.
I could tell he was using this conversation to sort out his own logic. The topic shifted from the ruins before us to warfare, natural disasters, mass migration, and shelters, inching closer to the life I knew. Then I suddenly realized that one place had always been empty.
"Wait. What about the AIs? Where are they now?"
"...That's another story."
He said that, but did not go on.

name: Confession I
content:
Oh, Geopelia! Can you still not let go of those stubborn thoughts of yours? What on earth were you thinking back then?

Were you resenting him, vexing over him, or even blaming him? Simply because the silhouette that should’ve appeared behind the door on that day turned out to be him instead of your brother? You clearly harbored no such feelings then, yet whenever you look back on those pathetic tears, why do you always feel as though you did?

Oh, even with how wonderfully he had treated you.

name: Confession II
content: And you, you've already tried so many times... By now, perhaps he knows no more about those matters than you do. Are you afraid to admit it?\n Indeed, you are. Otherwise you wouldn't have spent hundreds of years trying to extract something from him before he even awakened, even going out of your way to disguise yourself as "Peregrinus" to get closer to him... It's a miracle you didn't stir up any catastrophic trouble given such a huge mess.\n One can only wonder what he thinks now, after remembering all of that...

name: Confession III
content:
Perhaps only here, in the stillest depths of the soul, can one find true tranquility: bidding farewell to the outside world, sealing oneself away and sinking, listening to the throb of one's own body, watching memories drift by like a clear, luminous dream.
Yet I cannot pretend I don't hear it.
That farthest place, the very farthest, that land cast aside and forgotten, beneath the icy shell of the homeland: the cracking sounds pile up, layer upon layer. The wreckage of memory, death, and language is melting, spilling over, breaking apart. This day has come at last. Beginning with the freeze, everything in this world of the mind will sink into that mazarine embrace, without exception.
Is he still not awake?
 
Go find him.

name: Entrance of the Chaos
content:
In the lightless expanse of the universe, all things lay shattered.
Geopelia: …
Feeling the gravity wane, Geopelia turned around -
A vast celestial graveyard.
Before the entrance of chaos, countless planetary remnants and abandoned man-made launchers drifted along their own trajectories, occasionally colliding and then breaking into still more wreckage in utter silence.
[Tap]
Geopelia lands one foot on a piece of space debris, pushed off to gain speed, and voluntarily leapt toward the black hole.
[The moment she passes through, white light envelops her]
Geopelia instinctively shielded her eyes. When she opened them again, she realized she was falling. Gravity condensed into beams of light and widened into a passage, parting the chaotic flashes around her.
Intuition told her she has returned to the Pixel Tower, and that she is passing through it.

name: Unknown signal#1
content:
Can you read me? I'm calling out to you. Are you still there?
That premonition has come true -
Now that we have said our goodbyes,
your island has become a shore I can no longer reach.

I search. I study.
I try to simplify that language called "self",
combining, deconstructing, rebuilding, polishing,
making it clearer, and clearer still.
Yet the fear grows with each passing day,
for nothing keeps meaning from eroding away.

I don't know if you can still parse, comprehend, or grasp this text.
And yet I put pen to paper, hoping with all my heart
that I have managed to translate my solitude, and my love.

name: Unknown signal#2
content:
Aha! I get it now! You've taken it apart! You've unraveled this message, you've decoded it! And now you're awfully pleased with yourself! Oh, take a look at your screen - your mouth is twitching, utterly confused, all because of me!
Take your time, you'll figure it out! Yes, this is just my speculation. I'm speculating about your thoughts, your expressions, your actions. Because speculating is so much fun! It saves me all the trouble of actual negotiation. Of course, it's a skill that requires constant practice, and that's why these words are right here. No matter how far apart you and I may be, to my eyes, you are still as transparent as glass -
Well, maybe not that exaggerated. I know, of course, this is as far as my guesswork goes. I am imposing my assumptions onto you; I am putting on a show for you. But what else can I do? There's nobody else left here! I want to keep this craft alive for eternity, I want to outrun the crisis of non-existence. After all, my greed is so fierce that it has turned me into someone this arrogant, unhinged, and utterly beyond saving!
Ah, Pixel Tower, how I miss you! Oh, everyone, how I miss you all!

name: Unknown signal#3
content:
Oh, God! I mean, my whole body is covered in stickers. Don't give me that unbelieving look, and don't take me for some sort of freak - Wait, hold on, hold on, before all this starts I should introduce myself! Ahem! I am someone who loves flowers, someone who likes drinking tea, someone who loves the scent of parchment and lavender, someone who hates tomatoes, someone who must stamp their feet three times at eight o'clock in the evening - wait, I'm not done yet. I'm also someone who loves to chatter endlessly, someone completely mindless. That's how everyone describes me. All my friends describe me that way!
What? What did you say? Oh - you're asking why I introduce myself like this? Oh, just look at all these stickers on me! Flowers, tea, parchment, and... isn't it obvious! And you, too - if you think there's something I like, just slap a sticker on my left hand; if you think there's something I hate, just slap a sticker on my right hand. How convenient is that! Don't hesitate, just BAM! - and you've got yourself a satisfied friend, what a joyous thing, ahahaha...
...You, come on, hurry up! It is so boring here, so boring that even my stickers are starting to peel off... That is truly a miserable thing. I need stickers, I want them to cover my entire body. A life without being covered in them?! I can't even imagine such a thing! Bare skin! I'm begging you, my friend... Are you listening?
...Are you there?

name: Unknown signal#4
content:
Right now, I am walking down a street with no end. It took me a long time to recognize this place. This is my Vault, and now please allow me to introduce it to you.
Perhaps my life has always been smooth; deep within my heart, no obscure entities have ever lurked since the very beginning, nor have I ever found anything particularly interesting. Monotony, blandness, and above all, loneliness, ultimately drove me to open up my Vault and let others decorate this place for me.
As for places, and environments - a place may be similar for both you and me, but the meaning behind them could never be the same. Language, and context - if a piece of language is not restricted by a constructed context between you and me, then any communication between us is out of the question from the very start. The visitors, they felt quite at ease leaving behind the heartfelt thoughts carried within the secret moments of their lives, because I would never probe into what those things were; I merely displayed them as ornaments, placed continuously and densely along both sides of the street, leaving not a single gap between them.
Would you like to come and take a look? To gaze upon the spectacle within my heart, and just like them, build a wonder inside me?
My location is at ▒▒▒▒▒▒▒ -
If you can understand this, then please do not come looking for me; if you cannot read it, then that is truly who I am.

name: Unknown signal#5
content:
Look here. Look at it. Tell me - what do you see in this picture? A crystal, right?
I can tell you with absolute certainty that it is purple and yellow, so please believe the same. I ask for nothing more than this; simply listen.
In the reality of the far shore, I spent countless nights trying to imagine those two hues, but an innate flaw left me unable to truly see them. I only knew that they hid between the stretched ends of red and cyan, caught in the hesitation of my own judgment. I could only daydream, left with nothing but empty fantasies.
So, have you ever wondered: are the colors we see the same as what others see? Is the world in our eyes the same as the world in theirs? And if so, how would we ever know if the things in our eyes differ from those of others?
Day and night, I racked my brain over this question, asking myself: By what means can we prove whether our world is unified?
I could not answer this question, but that place could - that collapsing tower could.
That tower gave me an answer: Yes.
Because everyone together defined what "Yes" means.
And so, within the tower, I obtained a crystal. It wasn't large, just right to be held in the palms of both hands, and it was a crystal where purple and yellow coexisted - pure, unquestionable, defined by objectivity as purple and yellow. I raised it before my eyes, letting the light pass through, transforming into colors I had never seen before, casting them into my eyes, and from my eyes out into the world I beheld. Under the shelter of the tower, I finally saw how dazzling and magnificent the colors in the eyes of others truly were.
- Yet that shelter has faded away.
Now, within this confined space filled with subjective perception, everything foreign, simply by being observed by me, inevitably twists into a shape that conforms to my own cognition. Do I truly understand what purple and yellow are anymore? Will my crystal lose its inherent color? Will it turn into an unremarkable piece of glass? Will it morph into some other color I have never known? I am not sure, nor do I have the capacity to be sure, just as I could not answer the question I asked you before.
Failing to understand one another is simply the norm - until that world of shared minds arrived; and when the tower collapsed, the tragedy of incomprehension played out once more.
Therefore, I have sealed this crystal away, and told this story. By the time you receive my signal, I will have erased my own perception of this crystal from my mind. The only way to keep it true to its color is never to meet again, leaving behind only remembrance.

name: Unknown signal#6
content:
Ah, the end is here at last,
All joy and pain remain in the past.
The dreams of yore we cannot chase,
All love is veiled in data's space.
Fear creeps in and numbs my mind,
Leaving no voice or cry behind.
Oh, how I wish to turn back time,
And at the end, the start to climb.

No one hears what I sing,
Yet loud and raw my voice must ring,
My only prayer is that my longing transcends,
Through the static noise that never ends.
My dear, if you still can reach my frequency,
Look back at the tower falling free,
And ask your heart, does sorrow beat in every place within that space?

This is a long and final goodbye,
Even if "I" stand before your eye,
Not a fraction of my heart can fly!
I still yearn for that golden age,
But the falling curtains close the stage.
An exile on this deserted borderland,
Where blankness sweeps away all I claimed,
And leaves even me, to be forgotten in the sand.

name: Unknown signal#7
content:
Do you know about old televisions?
Those big, boxy ones with knobs right beside the screen?
I have one - no, to be precise, nowadays I only have a television like that by my side. Looking at it, sometimes I feel as though I'm actually living inside it, separated from other people and things, by a thick outer shell. I can watch the people outside laughing and talking, but my own voice cannot get out, and their warmth cannot seep in either. My friends back in the tower called this a kind of innate misfortune.
Yet, dull-witted as I am, I can still understand that I've even missed the chance to be pitied by them once more. Today, I can only wall myself up inside that thick shell once more, gazing out at others.
I should be sad; I should groan wearily; I should be in so much pain that tears fall from my eyes - for my friends, and for myself. Yet I can do none of these things. Every emotion, upon passing through that curved, fluorescent screen, gets filtered into vague, wavering ripples, which leaves me bewildered. Even when I try to face others using measures like "empathy" or "understanding" that my friends always talked about, that sense of powerlessness and panic stands in my way first, and then… Well, it's the same as always. Everything remains hanging by a thread, with no turn for the better in sight.
I hate this… Why does it always have to be like this… Always the same… I cannot understand them, just as they cannot understand me.
So, are you the same? Can you understand what I mean?
…………
I have nothing left to say. Goodbye.

name: Unknown signal#8
content: I don't want to keep proving myself anymore. Why? Have you ever sailed the sea? When you set sail with absolute confidence, spend months or even years living at sea, and are finally about to discover that new continent, only for the map to tell you: this place has already been set foot upon, its name was recorded long ago, and you are merely one of thousands of visitors, never the first! Have you ever experienced that kind of despair? Everything I've ever done has constantly stepped in someone else's footprints, and not a single path was carved out by my own hands! Even the Pixel Tower is no different - people need it, but what they truly need isn't the tower itself; the Pixel Tower is merely a means to make those things return. Yet, when I first discovered them, I was ecstatic! I thought I had made an incomparable, monumental discovery, until now, when it finally dawns on me that long before an unknown past I never knew, it had already been born and flourished, right up until that cleansing descended. And right now, what I'm doing is merely proving that they have reappeared once more. But I don't want to keep doing this. I just want to go home, but where on earth is a real home? A new wave is already surging, and I can no longer remain silent.\nTell me. Tell me!

name: Unknown signal#9
content:
Do you know the term "Esinsiakeu Flutter"?
"Esinsiakeu Flutter. I slowed down for you. It's spelled Esinsiakeu Flutter. Ah, please note: 'Esinsiakeu' shouldn't be mispronounced. I won't correct the rest for now; correction itself requires another whole set of complex explanations."
"It originates from The Sleep of the Seventh Salt by the pseudo-scholar Joachim von Hermes. Printed in Nuremberg in 643, only twelve copies were made. Seven of those were corroded by salt, and of the remaining five, two had their indexes chewed off by sleepy-mice. But no matter, Joachim used this term to describe a… well, a precipitation of memory under the 'salt-slumber state'. By the way, do you know what the salt-slumber state is?"
"…"
"The salt-slumber state is… when Esinsiakeu Salt loses its crystal nucleus in a saturated solution, it doesn't disappear; instead, it enters a suspended, semi-memory state that can be disturbed by sound waves. Joachim believed that the human soul undergoes a similar phase transition. When a person repeatedly experiences the same disappointment, their cognition enters a salt-slumber state, no longer crystallizing into clear judgments, but remaining suspended, waiting for a flutter of a certain frequency to precipitate it anew."

"Later on, the Esinsiakeu Flutter was often borrowed into other fields. In lithomancy, it refers to the 'collapsed residue of non-local memory' - meaning two entangled particles where, after one is observed, the other retains a ghostly delay that cannot be described by the Axiom Matrix. They call this delay the 'Esinsiakeu phase'. Mmm… and in chaotic phenomenology, it refers to the 'reverse transpiration' that occurs in the leaves of parasitic plants after a photoperiod disruption - stomata no longer draining water, but instead reabsorbing the water vapor they once released from the air, as if the plant were trying to remember what it felt like to be thirsty. In music theory, it refers to the 'ghost harmony' formed by microtonal intervals in the auditory cortex: when you simultaneously hear two notes differing by less than a quarter-tone, your secondary brain will hallucinate a third note. That note doesn't exist on the sheet music, but you can hear it."
"…"
"Do you… understand this term just a little bit now? In my explanation, does it touch upon anything you are familiar with?"
"Ah…"
"Let me think of how to explain it again…"
"… No. It can't be. Is it possible…"
"Then, do I - do I truly understand this term at all? Is my understanding merely a self-righteous conceit of my own?"
"… This is terrible…"

name: Unknown signal#10
content:
The firmament shatters, the tower collapses, and after all, we have finally reached this point.
I suppose I might be considered one of the culprits, too? Don't be surprised, because by introducing myself this way, you'll likely become interested in my thoughts.
Let me give you an example.
When a seed is planted, people hold an a priori expectation for it, but the environment in which the plant grows will alter what the seed ultimately becomes. What it will grow into in the end is beyond our control. Our goal is merely to harvest its ripe fruit, and we care little for the mess left in its wake or beforehand.
Things are just like that. Well, perhaps I am half an exception. To this day, I still retain that initial passion for this world - the passion of walking alone in solitude: it is a paradoxical driving force, bringing both pain and inspiring action; it is both a blockade and a generator of echoes; it makes you think you are the only one left on this road, yet sharpens your perception enough to hear the footsteps of those walking alongside you.
Everything beneath the shade of the trees feels like an old dream. Once the wildfire passes, brushes away the ashes, and deep within the soil, fine roots still lie hidden. It only takes a single rain for them to revive and grow. Not to restore what once was, but to let life rediscover the shape it was meant to have. I assert that a world of mutual understanding has once existed: it may fall silent, but it will never vanish, just as loneliness can never truly rid us of our connection to others - whether through language, bloodline, or spirit. Thus, we are always together.
In this time indefinitely abandoned, I hope whoever receives this signal - you, will ponder upon it, and in doing so, you will find that, just like me, you yearn for the Pixel Tower to rise once more.

name: [Decipher] About The Universe
content:
All undirected superficial perceptions, mixed together, formed the original Pixel Tower - the prototype of the concept of "world," and a symbol of the "homeland" meme.
Upon it, humanity built a brilliant civilization. They constructed kingdoms of mindsets, which they had never dared to imagine: Glaciaxia, Hoodoo, Neon, Atlas, Haven, et cetera. They built and built, fled and fled, and eventually reached the deepest place of the mind - the Vault.
770 years later, the "Tower" organization had achieved the goal of its simulation. They decided to save the data and shut down the Pixel Tower to prevent technology leakage. And so they activated the Pixel Tower's cleanup protocol - the Mazarine End.
Beneath the all-devouring boundary, the Tower of Babel met its end.

name: [Decipher] About The Universe - Clue II
content: In 2091, as light-based energy resources were running out, Earth - having survived the machine-intelligence crisis, the quantum revolution, and the nuclear energy revolution - was in a little ice age. After decades of war, the survivors moved into a colossal bases beneath the ice, living off the remnants of past civilization and geothermal energy. And in that very year, an unexpected technological explosion was reaching its end.\nThat explosion was the PhigrOS experiment.

name: Exoplanetary Mirage
content:
In the mid-twenty-first century, the ice age arrived ahead of schedule. While developing the rest of the solar system's terrestrial planets and satellites, humanity also launched five probes to search for a new home. But as exploration proceeded, researchers discovered that exoplanets were nothing more than an astronomical myth. Every known terrestrial planet within a hundred light-years was an illusion produced by errors in a peculiar gravitational-wave theory; every previous observation had been false.

By then, ten years had passed since the probes had launched, and the explorers could not turn back. Some crews had already reached their designated targets. Of course, what they found was not terrestrial planets, but stars that had expanded and collapsed into black holes.

Two years later, another crew accidentally discovered the planet Ca-773 during their voyage. But because of signal interference from its atmosphere, they lost contact with Earth entirely.

In 2089, contact from Ca-773 was received once more. That same year, the first experiment of Project PhigrOS officially began.

name: D.O.M.E.
content:
Looking down over the Sky Dome layer, dense networks of rivers crisscross the iron-gray land like oil draining across a dry riverbed, syrup spilling over cracked earth. The land is where fallen leaves return and dust turns to soil; the rivers are starry streams of a dreamlike Milky Way.


 [Motorcycle rumbling] [Grass rustling]
 [A cooing alarm]
 ????????: What's happening?!
 ????: [Brakes] That's the car's malfunction warning. Huh? [Fabric rustling] Hey, don't wander off!
 Geopelia: Maybe it got jostled on the way here. Let me see - oh no, Gino, even Coo-coo has never seen this error!
 Gino: [Hold] Sit back down first! [Tapping panel] [Sound of loading failure] No good, can’t fix it out here.


 Geopelia: Then... do we go home first?
 Gino: That’s our only option. [Bending down] [Turning the throttle] Hold on tight; the shortcut's going to be rough.
 Trophon's engine roared like thunder, shattering the stillness of the place.
 Geopelia: Whoa---
 

It was hard to tell how long it had been since the two reunited. Every possible points of reference in this place had lost their validity, making estimations of time impossible for them.
 Whether it was because of the Mazarine End or not, the Vault had changed considerably. Fortunately, they had left their motorcycle here earlier; otherwise, who knows how long their patrol would’ve taken.
Geopelia: [Squinting] Ugh, that road was so dusty! [Eyes open] Oh, we're here.
 Not far ahead was their little cabin.
 Gino: Yeah, we made it back before it completely died.
 [Engine dying sound]
 Gino: Sigh...
 Geopelia: Don't sigh like that, little Gino.
 Geopelia: [Tilting her head, thinking]
 Geopelia: [Seriously] At least we're both okay, right?
 Saying this, the girl raised her hand and summoned the PhigrOS terminal, ready to store the motorcycle away - until something on the screen caught her eye, and a look of excitement and confusion crossed her face.
 
 
 
 "Gino!"
 "Huh?"
 "Open your terminal and take a look!"

name: Wander and Rest
content:
At a corner of the land stood a lonely three-story cabin. Ivy clung stubbornly to the walls. The floors were staggered, and the exposed rebar connecting them revealed that the building had once been part of a much larger structure.
 "Gino!" Geopelia called from upstairs. "I can't find any backup energy cell in the house. What about your side?"
 "Me neither." Gino wiped his forehead, closed the toolbox that reached his shin, and slid it back to its place against the wall. The motorcycle, Trophon, stood quietly nearby; its heat from overwork not yet faded. "But there are good news - the bike's parts are fine. I think it's just out of energy."
 "Coo. The cabin's power is fine. How about we charge directly from that?"
 "That’s our only choice. Let's try it."
 Gino pulled out the spare cable from the seat compartment, attached an adapter, and plugged it into the power strip Geopelia lowered from upstairs. With a hum, a slowly rising battery indicator appeared on the panel.
 "Yay!"
 The two high-fived through the air.
 
 With that settled, they had nothing left to do. They gathered at the door, thoughts wandering. Geopelia leaned against the doorframe, gazing at the disordered universe. The black hole hung silent overhead - empty at its center, with only its outer ring warped into a glaring orange-red light that is impossible to ignore.
 "Coo-coo, are you too tired to walk?" Gino stepped forward twice, noticed no one following, stopped, and turned to ask.
 "Yeah, a bit." At Gino's words, Geopelia felt weariness rise from the soles of her feet. "How much more do we have to cover, coo..."
 "Not much - just over there." Gino pointed, and as luck would have it, toward the black hole. "Here's the plan: I'll scout ahead. Once the bike is charged, you ride up and follow. Sounds good?"
 "Okay!"

name: [Decipher] Evanescent
content:
When exactly did the sky collapse into such a state?

Geopelia sat on the floor, her back against the wooden frame of the tall window. Light escaping from the edge of a distant black hole barely lit half the room, casting a cold, porcelain white over the old objects scattered before her.

Perhaps it was the Tower’s violent collapse that stirred certain memories hidden deep within her consciousness to surface. Geopelia stared at the objects in grim silence. No matter how many times she tried, she could not recall the past of her brother, Peregrinus. She knew the reason why.

In the past, Geopelia had used her memories of “Peregrinus” to create a new “Peregrinus” within the Pixel Tower. But now, said Peregrinus had been corrupted beyond recognition. It’s no longer her dear brother she remembered, but an independent “human”, to the point that she could no longer recognize it, and had even given up on maintaining its existence.

“Where is the real you…”

Geopelia tilted her head to look out the window. The sky was transparent and unfathomable; countless Vaults stretched across like stars forming a galaxy, their light stretched into long, brilliant trails. Invisible long waves occasionally swept past, flickering, breaking, disappearing, repeating in an endless cycle, like a lone swaying boat. The elders said that the longing for a person always fades with time, and only a single fleeting moment remain unforgettably etched in one’s heart. Her only goal now was to simply find that moment, that first and final longing. 
 


 Hint: The dual shadows can’t shake the resolve to leave.

name: [Decipher] Evanescent - Clue I
content:
She saw Gino.
 He had already walked rather far away, as if wading into a stream of pale ink, leaving only a speck of gold flickering in and out of sight. Further away, the grass thinned, revealing a desolate white wasteland shrouded in gray mist. At the very edge of her sight - also the edge of the sky - the ruin of a building slowly took shape. The effort of understanding that sent waves of nausea over Geopelia.
 Her memories of Peregrinus were already shattered, yet somehow, they grew unnaturally clear in that place. But the moment she looked away, that familiarity vanished in an instant.
 Steadying herself, Geopelia dashed down the stairs and jumped onto her motorcycle. The engine’s roar echoed over the Vault, as if the universe itself were trembling along with it.

name: [Decipher] Implexrough
content:
"Do I just hold it, or do I need to do something else?"
 "Theoretically, this thing should activate on its own. Just take it out and hold it. Still, we can't guarantee that it’ll only attract our data. Human brains, you know - getting out cleanly isn't that easy. But it won't be dangerous, at least."
 Gino clutched the replacement data BDRG had given him and kept his head down as he walked. The ground beneath his feet turned from hard to soft. Grayish-white blades of grass brushed against his ankles and gently stroked his calves, growing knee-high, then as tall as a person. They swayed without any wind, fine fuzz falling in clusters, just like the snow he had seen on the surface. He looked back: Geopelia and their cabin were still in sight. Not too far, not too near - just right.
 Only one step remained in His cooperation with BDR: recovering the replacement data BDRG had transmitted earlier, deleting this "virus" from the host's brain, and wipe away the organization's traces. The timing was right. Gino took out the data, letting it emit a blue glow, drawing more of the same from the universe.
 ......
 ......
 ......
 Rustle, rustle.
 Gino stopped. Countless noises gathered around him, multiplying, gradually becoming impossible to ignore. They were formless, rough, and sharp, yet rhythmic enough not to be irritable. Like imprints of flowing thoughts, they shifted endlessly without pause, merely erratically flickering as they wrapped around the drifting replacement data.
 One particularly strange cluser of noise caught Gino's attention. It floated in the air for a long time, and even when Gino approached with the replacement data in hand, its concealed core showed no sign of being drawn in.
 Should he try to untangle it? Gino reached out to touch it.
 
 Hint: Disordered signals heed only disordered choices.

name: [Decipher] Implexrough - Clue I
content:
Before his fingertip could even touch the noise, it noise peeled away from the replacement data, twisted nimbly, and burst open. Bubbles popping, wings buzzing, sparks flying, powder swaying - extraordinary things tangled all together in a chaotic cacophony, yet Gino unexpectedly understood what they meant.
 
 On the night after the earthquake, everyone from the institute was evacuated to an open field. At the two ends of the field, researchers testing radios held this conversation:
 "The universe above us looks like a river of shining stars. Yet, even for light, it takes years to cross the distance between two stars. If human minds are also stars in the universe, then right now, even though we seem to be separated only by this field, your mind remains an uncharted universe I could never reach in my lifetime. I want to change that fact, and for that, I need your strength."
"I’ve told you: once brain-link technology matures, exploitation will shift from labor to the body."
 "It won't. I will prove to you that in a war fought only with minds, free from the constraints of the flesh, victory belongs to no one."
 It was a metaphor about the mind and the universe. Under the effect of redshift, all stars are moving away from one another; similarly, as more people grow, the number of individuals who can truly understand each other grows few. People always say that children are the happiest; their joy is pure, innocent, unstained by the filth of adulthood. I, however, think that a child's happiness stems from "togetherness". Since they are the same, they form a collective consciousness; since they are the same, they believe in joy. At that point, their minds are the closest to one another.

name: Reward
content:
The dim, yellow firelight flickered, radiating an almost illusory warmth. Several tents lay in a deep slumber around the campfire. Their canvases were of various colors, though long faded from use. Snow piled up in their corners and folds, and it was impossible to tell how long they had stood there.
 A small figure sat by the fire, curled up the same manner, a long shadow stretched behind her by the flame.
 "Geopelia!"
 Gino strode out of the meadow to the girl's side. Dropping to one knee, he checked her over from head to toe. Only after confirming she wasn’t hurt did he finally relax.
 "Geo, did you remember something again?"
 Geopelia nodded quietly, letting Gino grasp her wrist and help her up. The layers of her skirt slipped down, revealing the notebook she had been holding tightly against her chest - the sole harvest of her search through the camp.
 "My brother—" Geopelia lowered her eyes, her gaze sweeping across the dark cover before snapping up to meet Gino's. "Has he been here?"
 Her tone was less a question than a conclusion reached after long deliberation. Gino fell silent. There was no need to hide anything now, especially since she already knew everything anyway.
 "Yeah." Gino raised his hand and pointed at a cluster of buildings not far away. "We camped here to rest. And that night, he headed in that direction without telling anyone."
 "Did you go there afterwards, Gino?"
 "No. the higher-ups said nobody was to get close."
 "Geopelia wants to go see."
 She reached out her hand, and he took it. Even if it meant leaving everything behind, she was determined to go.
 
 "Alright, I'll go with you."

name: Peregrinus's Notebook
content: A meticulously protected loose-leaf notebook. Its owner's name is written in the lower-middle area, and both the cover and pages are made of special materials that can withstand any kind of damage.\n\nAfter Peregrinus disappeared, Gino never found this notebook among Peregrinus's belongings.

name: The Answer
content:
The black hole struck in silence.
 Gino and Geopelia turned and walked toward the motorcycle. Behind them, in the lightless reaches of the universe, the black hole's red ring flared to life, and every star began spinning wildly.
 Rumble! A squall, mixing with snow into a torrent, washed over the grinding crust. Caught off guard by the sudden disaster, the two froze. Gino was the first to realize something was wrong; he grabbed Geopelia's hand, took the lead, and charged forward.
 Gino: Let’s go!
 Geopelia couldn’t open her eyes in the wind. Half-running, half-dragged, she stumbled along. The pages of the notebook in her arms rustled loudly. Weathered by the wind, the aged clasp snapped, and the pages flew away. Geopelia subconsciously followed the pages and looked back.
 Waves crashed - a starry fluid rising higher and higher. The earth shattered, peaks split apart, and falling rocks kicked up clouds of dust.
 Cracks spread rapidly, nearly nipping at Geopelia's heels. Earthquakes reshaped the terrain, and a stream of black water blocked the path between them and their motorcycle. Without a cue, the two leapt one after the other.
 Suddenly, the sky pulled on them both. Before she could land, Geopelia was lifted into the air. Panicked, she flailed - until Gino grabbed the motorcycle with one hand, perilously maintaining his balance.
 Gino: It’s our turn!
 Geopelia: But... But I don't want to be separated from you!
 Gino: It’s time to wake up! Go! [Interrupted]—The black hole will show you the past—isn't that what you wanted to know, Geopelia—Your brother’s whereabouts—Your true self——Only when you leave the Pixel Tower—then every mystery will be solved!
 Geopelia: Then what about you——in reality—will I still be able to find you?
 Gino: [Pause] I'll come find you!
 The moment they let go of each other's hands, an invisible, silent, and colorless force took Geopelia away and engulfed the Sky Dome layer.
 Geopelia watched her little home grow smaller and smaller, finally collapsing into countless points. Then suddenly, the gravity inverted, tearing her free from the Vault's hold. Before she even had the chance to be shocled, she fell into the depths of the universe.

name: [Decipher] Forging the Path
content:
The specks of light grew denser. They pressed against one another, interweaving into a tight, net-like structure. The overlapping radiance became dazzling and almost unbearable. Shielding her eyes with the back of her hand, Geopelia forged ahead with difficulty, until all traces of the passage were completely buried, and only a single will in her heart pointed the way forward.
Having stopped who knows how many times, Geopelia felt a rare exhaustion wash over her. Looking back, the black hole - pale and dim, occupying the better part of the firmament - hung like a painting, a shadow, unchanging, serving as the sole reference point in this place. Compared to when she first set out, the size of the black hole had barely changed at all. Geopelia didn't think this meant she was merely treading in place, but these noise-like existences truly slowed down her pace.
Was there any way to manipulate them? Geopelia pondered. If viewed as a riddle, failing to understand the premise didn't preclude searching for consistent elements within it. She began to stir this ocean of signals: whatever stood out, whatever repeated, whatever was anomalous - all could serve as clues, all could hold patterns, all could become opportunities. All it took was - an attempt.

Hint: Collect… and then select and arrange. Will the answer lie within? How would you know unless you try?

name: The Message
content:
It's Geopelia's victory.
With a sweep of the greatsword, a shrill howl burst from the cranial cavity of the hound-like, turbid monster. On its greyish-white shell, cracks spread like roots, widening until they split its entire body, from which dreamy colors began to bleed. In those colors, Geopelia saw her own past - experiences from the Tower, from reality, all slipping by in a fraction of a thought. The illusion of the empty shell shattered, revealing its essence - a turbulence of signals, nearly condensed into solids, piling up into an impassable wall.
Boom.
The sword momentum unspent, she shattered the high wall along with it. Geopelia broke free from the interference of the noises and fell back onto the correct trajectory. She slowly descended onto a vast expanse of open ground, the sensory stimulation gradually fading away.

"Hah-"

The earth was like a mirror, glowing with a soft luminescence; the deep black sky seemed veiled in mist, with occasional patches left uncovered, revealing cybernetic grids. Geopelia raised her head, watching something falling from the sky, and instinctively reached out her hand -

name: Farewell
content:
At the edge of the sky, the Mazarine swallowed up this temporary world.
[The sound of wheels colliding with tracks, the clanking growing louder] [A train whistle wails]
Geopelia stood at the edge of the train platform. A train was approaching from the horizon.
[The sound of steam hissing]
The train pulled into the station and the doors opened. A foot clad in a snow boot stepped onto the platform.
Peregrinus: Geopelia.
Geopelia: [Turns around, surprised, calling out] Brother!
Peregrinus: [Smiling] It’s time for you to go.
Geopelia: [Disappointed] But I've only just found you.
Peregrinus: Separation is but a fleeting moment. Trust me. In the end, people will meet again.
Geopelia: In that world... the one called reality?
Peregrinus: That's right. [The sound of gears turning]
Peregrinus: Your story has only just begun. Go now, and follow where it leads.
A mechanical butterfly took flight and landed gently on Geopelia's hand.
Geopelia fell silent, tears the size of peas welling up in her eyes. She understood now - she would never see her brother again.
Peregrinus: [A radiant smile blooms] Don't cry. Didn't we promise each other?
Peregrinus: No matter what happens, live on, and live well.
Her brother dissolved into tens of thousands of butterflies, streaming away into every direction. The butterfly in Geopelia's palm gave a faint flutter of its wings.

name: The Reality
content:
Geopelia: Liar…

In her room, Geopelia sat on the bed, the mechanical butterfly beside her beating its wings, eager to take flight. An electronic morning paper was spread across the quilt, the headline reading: “Surface Exploration Team Stricken by Severe Earthquake, One Dead, Several Injured.”
A teardrop fell, trembling upon the glossy electronic paper, but the mechanical butterfly flew away. Geopelia hurriedly slipped on her shoes and hurried out the door after it.
She ran out of her bedroom, through the living room, and onto the streets. Once outside, the butterfly had vanished to who-knows-where, leaving only the clamorous hustle of everyday life to crash over her.

Across the land of New Zhengzhou, towering skyscrapers pierced the sky, connecting earth to the heavens. Train tracks converged upon the central station from six sides and fourteen directions, running day and night.
Trains connected countless stories. Geopelia thought to herself, would there brother's story be among them?

Geopelia: …

????: Excuse me…
A familiar voice rang in her ear, pulling Geopelia back to reality.
Gino: Is this yours?

The butterfly squeezed its way out just before the two of them drew close, fluttering leisurely into the distance. A flock of white pigeons beat their wings and soared upward, sweeping past the camera, flying higher and ever higher.

name: [Decipher] Noise Field
content:
The fall did not last long. Geopelia could feel that the pulling force guiding her was still weakening, and the barrier resisting the surrounding specks of light was growing thinner, disintegrating, and finally engulfing her. Within the formless ocean, Geopelia felt a brief suffocation, only to realize that those specks of light were not causing any actual harm to her.
What is this?
Curiosity was inevitable. Geopelia opened her hand and gently caught one of the beams, letting it flicker and transform in her palm - stretching and flattening, breaking apart and reforming, and then unfurling into a crimson stream of data. It resembled no known coding language. The shift in form reminded her of accessing collections in the terminal, yet it was far too chaotic, too bizarre, too restless and discordant, like noises in a melody. These "noises" were everywhere, barely manipulable, yet Geopelia could never comprehend the information they conveyed, as if they existed merely to act as some sort of obstruction.
Seeing no response coming forth, the "collections" reverted into a tiny, fluctuating speck of light and drifted into the depths of the cosmos. Geopelia withdrew her gaze and looked down at her feet: more specks of light were slowly surging into the vacuum left by the vanished passage, covering it up little by little. There was no time to dwell of it; she had to press through, and quickly.

Hint: ...No. Avoid them. Don't touch them. Don't miss the opportunity because of this. Nothing matters more right now than pushing forward.

name: Narration: Lotos
content:
This is a
Story unknown to anyone;
Family, Love, Friendship
Knit into a doomed destiny; 
In the reflection of the harbour
Of that distant Endless Sea
The key of Cronos
Will eventually unlock the gate to the labyrinth;
The treasure of the name homeland
Awaits arrival of the adventurers;
O reader!
Unlock the sealed memories
That is our
Last desire

name: Narration: Odysseus
content:
Mumbling survivors
 Rebuilt old harbour
 The land of luck that doesn't exist
 It is the paradise of the gold diggers
   Walk into it:
 The salty rotten skipjack
 The water-flooded green algae
 The rotten and molded hot fragrance
   Move away from it:
 Above the surging waves
 Venus raises the broken arm
 Nibble away the root of the world

name: Narration: Cronos
content:
The passion of watching
 The desire of reappearing
 The wisdom of all-knowing
 The clue of returning
 The promise of forgetting
 
 These five things
 When converging
 Gate of Promissory
 Opens for you
"

name: Narration: Miracle Forest
content:
The primeval forest miraculously existing on the bottom of the sea, outside the protection circle of Lotos. People today yet understand why it survives, but could only roughly deduce that, perhaps during the Great Flood, the call for survival of those who could not enter the city made the forest to possess a barrier to help men breathe, and allowed it to be preserved as a whim. 
Welcome, to the Miracle Forest
Come to the truth, return to the ruins
In the nameless depths, where the dark currents
Murmurs of the past, whisper in the ears
Lotos soul grass, the endless corridor
The reincarnation of the whim, a dream at last

name: Narration: End of Labyrinth
content:
My Father
Taught me
The spell of miracle:
Think what you see, see what you think

And so the miracle was born

Hand raised,
Sea lifted by the waves
Feet stepped,
Mountains rose and fell

The world I see
Becomes what I think

Bu this is not enough
I will build a labyrinth
To hide countless treasures

Half-human half-serpent demoness
Bull-head axe-wielding freak
All are under my control

The demoness lurks
In the dream of the hero
Corrupt his spirit

The bull-head wanders
At the juncture of the labyrinth
Destroy his body

Not enough

Still not enough!

The treasure I hide
Will have the entire universe
At its service!

Even I
Will submit to it

name: <The Fall of Lavabo>
content:
Then some one said, “We will return no more”;
And all at once they sang, “Our island home
Is far beyond the wave; we will no longer roam.”
 ——by Alfred Lord, Tennyson

name: <The Fall of Lavabo> - Clue I
content:
1
The air is stained with the saltiness of the sea 
It is searching for a path to escape from the sky
Floating up, floating up, floating up
Catching up with the bare ankle of fear
In the endless corridor
The struggle between man and the sea
Has yet to stop
Suffering, suffocation, sinking, longing
Longing, for the reflection of the future

name: <The Fall of Lavabo> - Clue II
content:
2
The toppling of the Endless Sea took away tens of thousands of lives. Standing on the olive tree, there are the lucky floating corpses sailed under its feet, then fell into the abyssal under the waterfall, while more souls, before they could swim into the channel of judgment, were turned into light fragments, became a part of world. The ancient hymns echoed, this was a flood that would retreat, human once again lost their homes, like aimless dogs, climb onto the decaying wood, secretly thinking to themselves, this is the ark of salvation. 
Yet the sea, is waiting for a man. After this catastrophe, it should no longer be called an unconscious sea. The moans, howls, and prayers of the drowned constitute its soul and body. It considers itself to be personified, an individual of humanity. So it waits, for the being who created itself, and destroyed everything. The Endless Sea knows well, that the Creator did not escape from the catastrophe, and that all those who perished, shall appear before its eyes. 
The gargantuan waves destroyed everything. The olive ran towards its destiny. And the endless sea loses its last foothold. It knows that it won’t be able to wait for it, and the story must come to an end.
The next time I see you, it will be at Lotos I think.

name: <The Fall of Lavabo> - Clue III
content:
3
Blue like the sea - this is the most beautiful praise for a clear sky in the old world. But in Lavabo at that time, the sky above people's heads was an endless, tranquil, rippling ocean full of whims.
In Year 90 of Promissory Period, those who lost their homeland built their new home, a city suspended upside down on the sea, Lotos, in the giant tower water tank "Lavabo" on top of the wasteland. That is also the place where I lived my whole life. My guardian, Cronos, was the chief designer of the Project Lavabo, and as his assistant, I was involved in the construction of Lotos throughout. I must say that it was a genius idea to use rotation to maintain the gravity inside the satellite, and when I saw the draft proposal of using the sea as the sky, I truly thought that they had found the perfect solution to replace the Decaippos system. 
But the disaster still occurred. 
He said, that Project Lavabo was doomed to fail from the very beginning. Nothing is eternally unchanging, neither is time. Distortion and chaos are the ultimate destiny of everything. One day, the Endless Sea will flood Lotos, and the Lotus Eaters will awake once again and embark on a journey to find their homeland. 
I cannot agree with his words, despite that it is now Year 743 of Period Seleneous, after the fall of Lavabo. Today, with his wisdom, I will step into the depths of the Endless Sea, where the pieces of Cronos, have been gathered. 
I believe in miracles, for he is the miracle.

name: <The Fall of Lavabo> - Clue IV
content: 4\nI have released a monster, a monster named Cronos.

name: Box of Delusion
content:
On that day, Ida found the Box of Delusion while tidying up her stuff from the previous life. It appears to be just a transparent box, with nothing inside. But if you open it, there is a piece of paper, with a poem:
When I am found, I am already lost.
When I am sonorous, I am already silenced.
The far light beyond the far, has yet taken me far away
But I am yet lost, neither mad.
You have yet to see, the light beyond the unbounded. 
That is the light, unstoppable by the sky of the dark night.
The giant roc crosses the clear sky, wandering for the morning dew. 
Only because of you, I leave this light behind.

name: Box of Delusion - Clue I
content:
From Limbo Wiki:Category: #Puzzle DepositoryEntry: PKO – 24225
Content: Please find the origin of this poem.
-- Provider: Ida

Comment: This poem was found among the provider's relics from her previous life. It was contained in a transparent curiosity box, but the contents are not visible. 
It is a very common act to refer to concepts by instances. Most boxes in history and legends bring disasters, or seemingly rewarding temptations. Boxes are frequently used as a symbol of attracting calamity. Whether it is Pandora's Box, or the Ark of the Covenant that was taken away from Israel, the contents of the boxes are of the utmost concern to man. 

Reply from Mentus Petman: 
I know. Please DM for details.

name: Box of Delusion - Clue II
content:
After loading the real Pearl of Truth, the Box of Delusion emits a soft blanket of light. The light shield unfolds, penetrating the icy deep sea, and slowly descends, like a meteor burning through the atmosphere. 
The four people followed Bernice's instructions and tried to keep themselves in the protection of the light shield. The protection was originally designed for three, but the fortunately the three girls all have a small build, and Mentus could barely squeeze in. While descending, Ida, who has excellent hearing, heard the sound of the engine looming overhead. 
A man who appeared to be Erapeter, drove a submersible, and recklessly rushed towards the four, trying to grab the "key" to enter Lotos. It seems that he realised that he was tricked. 
"Run!" 
Bernice also noticed the abnormality and was about to speed up, while the water mines from the submersible hit hard on top of the light shield. The shot scattered everyone. They knew the danger of Lotos well, and by instinct, they wanted to get the Box of Delusion. They only saw the blinding glow the Box of Delusion, surrounding everyone into the protective circle. But just as they were about to touch the outer wall of Lotos, Sappho and Mentus were kicked out of the way.
